name: Sudan
system_note: An army-led government at war with the RSF.
snapshot: The war between the army and the RSF, now in its fourth year, has caused the world's largest humanitarian crisis and effectively split the country in two.
culture: Sudan was home to the kingdoms of Kush and Meroë, whose pyramids outnumber Egypt's. Sudanese music, from the songs of Mohammed Wardi to the haqiba style, is loved across the Horn of Africa. Sufi dervishes still whirl in Omdurman on Friday afternoons. Arabic is the main language, alongside dozens of others in Darfur, Kordofan and the east.
society: More than 12 million people have been displaced by the war that began in April 2023, and famine has been confirmed in several areas. The RSF has been accused of genocide against the Masalit and other non-Arab groups in Darfur. Gold, much of it smuggled to the UAE, finances both sides. Khartoum was heavily destroyed before the army retook it.
situation: In 2019, Sudanese crowds toppled Omar al-Bashir after 30 years. The army and the Rapid Support Forces, a paramilitary grown from the Janjaweed militias of the Darfur genocide, promised a transition to civilian rule. Instead, in April 2023 their two leaders, army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, turned on each other. More than 200,000 people have died and the UN calls it the world's largest hunger and displacement crisis (AFP via Ahram).

The army retook Khartoum in 2025, but the RSF captured El Fasher, the last army stronghold in Darfur, that October, with mass killings that shocked the world. In 2026 the war moved to Kordofan. From mid-June, the RSF massed around El Obeid, a city of half a million that links Darfur to Khartoum, and hammered it with drones; the UN warned about 500,000 civilians faced the risk of atrocities and pleaded that "the horrors of El Fasher" must not repeat (Shafaq News). In late July the army pushed the RSF off the highway to Khartoum, easing the siege, and Dagalo responded by "unleashing" his fighters. The G7 demanded an end to the assault. US-led mediators have pushed a humanitarian truce, but Burhan has brushed it aside, and analysts say Emirati backing for the RSF, which the UAE denies, has blunted US pressure (RANE). The RSF runs a parallel "Tasis" government in the west, and Sudan is drifting toward partition.
power: No functioning constitutional order. The army-led government, based in Port Sudan and Khartoum, controls the east, north and centre; the RSF and its Tasis administration control most of Darfur and parts of Kordofan.
holders: General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan (army); Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, "Hemedti" (RSF).

update.html: The army's offensive from late July broke the RSF ring around El Obeid and pushed west into Kordofan, while the RSF and its SPLM-N allies opened a front in Blue Nile around Kurmuk. Drones are now the main killer of civilians: the UN counted 306 civilians killed by drone strikes between 1 and 21 October alone. US-led Quad diplomacy has produced a draft truce text but no ceasefire.
